clue.text: Wally, the pickpocket's son, gets credit

parts.note: dip is slang for a pickpocket
tick is British slang for credit, as in buying on tick

explanation.surface: A thief's boy finds himself trusted with a loan, and is called a fool for it.
explanation.walkthrough: Wally is British slang for a fool, and so is the answer; it is not a name here.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are British slang insults for a silly, foolish person.

clue.text: Judge finds detectives taken in by banker

indicators.note: taken in by means the detectives are held inside the banker

parts.note: a banker is crossword slang for a river, one with banks; the Dee is a river in Britain
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the British police detectives

explanation.surface: A judge finds police officers have been fooled by a financier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banker' wants to be a financier; it is a river, here the Dee.
explanation.definitionFit: To judge a matter is to settle or rule on it, reaching a verdict.

clue.text: Finished one small drink

parts.note: something finished is over and past
I is the Roman numeral one
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: Someone has downed a single small drink.
explanation.definitionFit: An aniseed-flavoured French aperitif, drunk diluted with water.

clue.text: To rail about a small breakfast utensil

indicators.note: about means the to-plus-rail pair goes round the next letters

parts.note: a railway track is a rail

explanation.surface: Someone complains loudly about a little breakfast gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rail' looks like the verb to complain; it is the noun. 'about' wraps the to-and-rail pair around A and S.
explanation.definitionFit: A toast rack is a slotted stand that holds slices of toast upright at the breakfast table.

clue.text: Caught droppin' curry in the sports pavilion

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
hanging down is drooping or dropping, and the apostrophe drops the final G
to curry a horse is to groom it with a currycomb

explanation.surface: A cricketer is out, caught, after spilling a curry in the pavilion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curry' wants to be the food; it is the verb for brushing a horse. A sports pavilion is the building at a British cricket ground where players change.
explanation.definitionFit: Players get changed in this room, which is the main part of a cricket pavilion.

clue.text: Dry American conspirator

parts.note: brut describes very dry champagne
US is short for American, as in US citizen

explanation.surface: A humourless American is plotting something.
explanation.walkthrough: Dry looks like a description of the American's manner; it is the wine term.
explanation.definitionFit: Brutus was one of the plotters who assassinated Julius Caesar, the classic example of a conspirator.

clue.text: Approach made quickly

definitions.meaning: a sprint or build-up before a jump or a bowl, or the period leading up to an event
to run something up is to make it hastily

explanation.surface: An approach was put together in a hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the lead-up to an event; the other is the phrasal verb for sewing something up fast.

clue.text: Manage after suffering in rehearsal

indicators.note: after places the word for manage behind the word for suffering

parts.note: a trial is an ordeal or suffering
to run a business is to manage it

explanation.surface: Running things after an ordeal during practice.
explanation.definitionFit: A practice performance or test before the real thing, done to check everything works.

clue.text: Keep one's place — international race in view

indicators.note: in means those letters sit inside the word for view

parts.note: sight means view, as in in sight
the TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A spectator holds their spot to watch a world-class race.
explanation.walkthrough: The TT is the famous Isle of Man motorcycle race.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay put and not move or act, holding one's position.

clue.text: Abandon players on holiday

parts.note: the cast of a show is its set of players
someone on holiday is away

explanation.surface: An instruction to leave the actors behind while they are off on vacation.
explanation.definitionFit: To cast away is to throw aside or desert, as a shipwreck leaves a sailor stranded.

clue.text: Measure third of volunteers first to get signed up

parts.note: an en is a printer's unit of measure

indicators.note: picks the third letter of the word volunteers

parts.note: 1st, with the digit read as the letter I, gives IST

explanation.surface: A plan to sign up volunteers by measuring a third of them first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' is written 1st, and crosswords read the 1 as I to give IST.
explanation.definitionFit: To enlist is to join up, especially for military service, by being put on the roll.

clue.text: Botched array disrupted energy source

indicators.note: disrupted means thrown into disorder, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bungled set of solar panels has cut off the power supply.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugars and starches in food are what the body burns for fuel.

clue.text: Implication makes many quarrel

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500, crossword shorthand for many
a rift is a falling-out or quarrel

explanation.surface: Reading between the lines suggests lots of people are arguing.
explanation.definitionFit: The drift of an argument is its general meaning or what it implies, as in catching someone's drift.

clue.text: Apple girl cooked for jazz musician

indicators.note: something cooked has been changed and reworked, so the letters of these words are shuffled

explanation.surface: A girl bakes an apple dish for a jazz player.
explanation.definitionFit: Stephane Grappelli was a French jazz violinist, partner of Django Reinhardt.

clue.text: Artist gets Bob endlessly agitated

parts.note: to gain is to get, so gets gives gains

indicators.note: endlessly means the name Bob loses its final letter

parts.note: rough water or a rough sea is agitated

explanation.surface: A painter makes someone called Bob more and more upset.
explanation.walkthrough: Bob looks like the person being agitated; it is just letters, cut short by 'endlessly' to BO.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Gainsborough was an eighteenth-century English portrait and landscape painter.

clue.text: Irate chum upset? He's quite ill

definitions.note: a noun for a person, someone afflicted by a joint disease

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An angry friend is in a state; is that because he is unwell?
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it names a sufferer from rheumatism, a person with painful joints.

clue.text: Artist sees women slither about

indicators.note: about here means moved around, so the letters of slither are rearranged

explanation.surface: A painter watches women crawl and slide around.
explanation.definitionFit: James McNeill Whistler was an American painter, known for the portrait of his mother.

clue.text: Web of global proportions to detain space traveller

parts.note: to intern is to detain or confine, as in wartime
ET is the alien from the Spielberg film, an extraterrestrial

explanation.surface: A giant spider's web is spun across the world to trap an alien.
explanation.definitionFit: The worldwide web is a computer network that spans the whole planet.

clue.text: Long to dress daughter with outstanding accessory

indicators.note: to dress something is to clothe it, so the word for long is wrapped around the daughter

parts.note: to long for something is to hanker after it
chief means foremost or outstanding

explanation.surface: A parent yearns to dress their daughter in some striking fashion item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to dress' puts D inside HANKER, giving HANDKER.
explanation.definitionFit: A pocket square or hanky is a small cloth carried as a fashion accessory.

clue.text: Player's remarkably agile around circuit

indicators.note: around means the scrambled letters surround the ring
remarkably suggests something unusual, so the letters of agile are rearranged

parts.note: a circuit is a round, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A sportsman is remarkably nimble as he runs round the track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts GALIE, the rearranged letters of agile, around O.
explanation.definitionFit: The keeper is the player who guards the goal in football or hockey.

clue.text: Church set in a hollow is respectable

indicators.note: set in means the church letters are placed inside the hollow

parts.note: a dent is a small hollow
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A chapel nestled in a valley looks perfectly proper.
explanation.definitionFit: Decent means proper and of good standing, acceptable by accepted standards.

clue.text: Curse deterioration in a weapon

indicators.note: in means the word for deterioration sits inside the weapon

parts.note: a sword is a weapon
wear is the gradual deterioration from use, as in wear and tear

explanation.surface: A curse has rusted a weapon over time.
explanation.definitionFit: A curse is an oath or profanity, a rude expletive.

clue.text: Old magistrate with a bill

definitions.meaning: a medieval English official, a chief officer of a town or manor
a female ruff, a wading bird, which has a beak or bill

explanation.surface: An old judge comes with a bill to pay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bill' looks like an invoice or a parliamentary bill; it is a bird's beak.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a medieval local official and the female of the ruff, a beaked bird.

clue.text: Doctor gets large elephant head? That's some beast

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor
OS is short for outsize, meaning large

indicators.note: head means the opening letter of the word elephant

explanation.surface: A vet is handed a huge elephant's head and marvels at the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: This large deer of northern forests is certainly a beast, so 'some beast' names one example.

clue.text: Singer allowed to keep a pub

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it inside, so the word for allowed holds the pub

parts.note: to let is to allow
an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: A performer has been permitted to run a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: Singer looks like a person; in crosswords it often means a songbird.
explanation.definitionFit: This small finch is a songbird, so it is a singer in crossword terms.

clue.text: Work the land in infamous prison

indicators.note: in means the farming word goes inside the word for infamous

parts.note: base means low or contemptible, as infamous conduct is
to till is to plough and cultivate soil

explanation.surface: Prisoners are set to farm work inside a notorious jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'infamous prison' reads as one phrase, but infamous gives BASE and only 'prison' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: The Paris fortress stormed in 1789 at the start of the French Revolution was a state jail.

clue.text: Betray woman more readily

parts.note: to rat on someone is to betray them
her refers to a woman

explanation.surface: A woman would happily sell someone out.
explanation.definitionFit: As in I would sooner go: the word means in preference, more willingly.

clue.text: Drills type of junction box

parts.note: to drill pupils is to teach them by repetition
a T-junction is a road junction shaped like the letter

explanation.surface: Electric drills and a junction box from a hardware catalogue.
explanation.walkthrough: A T-junction is where one road meets another end-on, the common British name for it.
explanation.definitionFit: A large wooden crate once used to ship tea leaves, later used for storage and moving house.
